items.title: Victoria Nagy, Chair, Heritage Centre Wellington re: 219 Farley Road,
notes: Fergus appeared in support of heritage designation of 219 Farley Road in Fergus. She indicated Heritage Centre Wellington values the property’s cultural heritage value and attributes and wants to protect it was demolition and prevent it from falling into further disrepair.

V. Nagy responded to questions regarding potential future uses for the farmhouse, and the Committee’s interest in collaboration with the developer/owner on a designation by-law that offers a variety of future uses.

items.title: Elora Rocks - Alcohol Pilot Extension
notes: Report from M. Tucker, Manager of Recreation Facilities THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approve the extension of the Elora Rocks Sr. Hockey Club’s pilot project permitting the service of alcohol in a designated section of the tiered seating area at the Jefferson Elora Community Centre for the 2025/2026 ice season, subject to the provisions outlined in the Township’s Alcohol Risk Management Policy and in compliance with the safe service plan as approved by the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO);

AND THAT staff continue to monitor the implementation of the safe service plan on a game-by-game basis, with authority to discontinue or require adjustments delegated to the Managing Director of Community Services.

notes: Report from K. Bettiol, Manager of Community Development THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves the Winter Experience Program funding allocations as recommended by the Economic Prosperity and Growth Advisory Committee and in report CS2025-28.
Councillor Jefferson requested staff provided an overview of the report regarding 219 Farley Road, Fergus.

D. Maiden, Senior Development Planner provided an overview of the report, indicating 219 Farley Road currently supports a historic stone farmhouse circa 1880 which was redeveloped into the Storeybrook subdivision. She noted the developer retained the farmhouse on a newly configured lot with the subdivision and it was zoned accordingly. D.
Maiden explained the property has been vacant for sometime and designation would prevent it from falling into further disrepair.

B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning & Development explained the mixed use zoning applied to the property to allow some commercial uses, a doctor’s office, etc., and responded to questions regarding other historical features associated with the property and the proximity of the parkette.

items.title: Municipal Accommodation Tax Implementation Update
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer
Presentation from K. Linton, Linton Consulting
D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided background on the Municipal Accommodation Tax Implementation, noting Council approved a 4 step approach as follows:
 Step 1 – Determine the appropriate structure for the MSC  Step 2 – Prepare the legislated required case study to establish the MSC
 Step 3 – Community engagement
 Step 4 – Preparation of necessary corporation, by-laws, and agreements

K. Linton, Linton Consulting provided background on the context and project objectives, the collaborative approach, the current state organizational model, municipal comparative practices, input from Council, the design principles and the preferred model. He outlined the next steps and responded to questions regarding the role of the Executive Director, the reporting structure back to Council and operational oversight, the goal of a well balanced, skill-based Board of Directors, regular communication and the establishment of a sustainable revenue stream for the MSC through MAT revenues, percentage of paid parking revenues and Ontario Lottery and Gaming revenues.

motions.item_title: Municipal Accommodation Tax Implementation Update
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approve the Municipal Service Corporation Structure for Economic Development and Tourism services, outlined in the Linton Consulting Services Inc. report included in report CAO2025-18; AND THAT Council approve proceeding to community engagement, preparing the required case study to establish a municipal service corporation, and to begin preparation of the necessary articles of incorporation, by-laws, and agreements; AND THAT Council approve the funding increase for the Municipal Accommodation Tax Implementation Project outlined in report CAO2025-18; AND THAT Council direct staff to report back to Council with engagement results, a draft case study, draft by-laws, and draft agreements prior to formally establishing a municipal service corporation.

motions.item_title: Housing Needs Assessment Follow Up Report
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington acknowledges the housing supply and affordability crisis in Ontario and supports the Township having a defined role in addressing this crisis going forward. AND THAT the Township's 2026 Budget and Business Plan incorporate the following in order to affirm the Township's future role in addressing the housing supply and affordability crisis: 1. Prepare a Township Housing Action Plan 2. Investigate the creation of a Township Housing Advisory Committee 3. Investigate potential applications to Wellington County for housing funding 4. Consider staffing implications of a Township housing mandate going forward
